utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Popaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your evidence will now continue. Please remember that the declaration you made at the beginning to tell the truth continues to apply to everything you say in court today. And counsel, Mr. Ackerman, will continue with his questions. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I've given a copy of his Albanian statement -- there, it's being handed to him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, would you open that up to, I think, the second page. You'll find some yellow highlighting in your statement there. Tell me when you've seen the yellow highlighting.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two other brothers, Nazmi and Nesim, who live --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have no idea what you're doing. I didn't ask you to read anything. I want you to find a page in that statement where I have highlighted in yellow some material. Maybe the usher could help you find it.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one is highlighted with red.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want one that's in yellow. Maybe the usher can help find it. It's on, I think, the second page of the statement. Now, you see the part that's in yellow. I'd just like you to read it out, please. This is your statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, so read out what you said there in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please provide the reference in English for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's on the top of page 3 of the English statement, the last sentence in the first paragraph on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you read it out loud, sir.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want you to read the part that's yellow. Can you see the part that's highlighted in yellow?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "I returned upstairs and went outside. I saw five tanks which were moving and taking up positions on a hill above Celine. I then told my family that the tanks had left."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. That's what's in your statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I told my family that the tanks had left the village, those that were near the mosque, that they went in the direction of the hill above Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, that's not what it says. You just read what it says. It says: "I saw the five tanks move off and take up positions on a hill overlooking Celine." You just read that to us; you didn't say you saw the three. Now, what I want to know is: Is what you said in your statement true or is that not true?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that they left, the tanks that went in the direction of Celine, above Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And according --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Bellacerka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And, according to your statement, that was five tanks; right?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five tanks entered the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So your statement is wrong. When you say, in your statement, "The five tanks moved off and took up positions on the hill overlooking Celine," that's wrong. Is that your testimony? Is that what you're saying under oath today?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I said in my statement and I'll repeat it today. The tanks that were near the mosque, they moved off in the direction of the hill above Celine. Those that went to the schoolyard, they remained there. Those that were at the mosque, they moved off in the direction of the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I think we'll get no further with that, sir, but the honourable Judges can see that that's not what you said in your statement, and I think that's good enough. Now, these tanks, wherever you want us to believe they were, never fired any weapons, did they?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not fire weapons at our village with tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, also in your statement, one of the things you told us is, you said: "I have, in the past, along with most of the village, given money and food to the KLA." What I would like to know is who was it in the KLA that you gave money and food to? Was it one person, several persons? Who was it you gave this stuff to, food and money?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We gave this in 1998. They were delivered to the KLA by the leader of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask you that. I asked you who you gave money and food to, not "we." Who did you give money and food to? Give me the name.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, not only me, my family, and others, we gave this money.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I know that others did and that's not my question. My question is: Who did you - you, Mr. Popaj, Mr. Sabri Popaj - who did you give money and food to? Give me a name.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mustafe Gashi was the village leader, and the people who were with him, they took this to the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. And that was just one time that you gave food and money?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One time. They asked one time, and we gave it one time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You've told us, about a week before the 25th of March, around the 18th of March, I guess, you say that some Serb police and soldiers arrived and started digging bunkers on a hill overlooking the village, and they had with them trucks and armoured vehicles. Do you remember that part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They entered Naim Fetoshi's house and they forced him to leave his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: For the registry, I'll be wanting to look at P615, page 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What steps did these people that came there with trucks and armoured vehicles take to camouflage these vehicles? What did they camouflage them with? What did they cover them with?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They dug the holes with excavators, they put them inside, and then they covered them with all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: They put the vehicles in the holes; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One APC went to Naim Fetoshi's courtyard, while the others, they went to the Breg or Brdo area. And they were firing from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now I would like the registry to zoom in, please, on this map. There's -- you can see a couple of villages below and to the village of Grahovac, almost right in the centre of the map. Now you -- now I want to go down. You can see Bela Crkva now and Celina. I want to zoom in, right in between those two villages. That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right, sir. You should be able to see on a map, in front of you now, your village of Bela Crkva and the village of Celina. And the first thing I'd like you to show us, by using a red pen or a blue pen or whatever color you want to use, the root that the tanks took, how they came into your village, and then where they went in the vicinity of Celina.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the road that goes to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. And what road did the tanks use when they entered your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The road from Xerxe to Rahovec. The tanks were above Bellacerka, and they entered Bellacerka from the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Would you just draw a line from where they entered to Celina, where they parked.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above the hill, between Bellacerka and -- you see this map is not exactly how it looks in the village. The hill was here, above Bellacerka, and the holes are still there; the positions that they took.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, we're not --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have not been covered yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We're not communicating, and I don't know whether it's a translation problem or what it is. But what I want you to do is with that pen draw a line along the route that the tanks travelled from the time they were -- no, you're not listening to me --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positions were above Bellacerka. The tanks -- well, you see, I don't understand this map. And I can't really draw a line because I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So this doesn't look like your village to you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can only read Bellacerka. I cannot recognise the roads here on the map; I don't understand them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you see --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positions are still there above Bellacerka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand that. Do you see Celina?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Celine village is very low here on the map, and in reality it's in line with Bellacerka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So one of two things, I guess, is possible: Either this map is wrong or you don't know anything about Bela Crkva and Celina. Are you actually from there?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was born in Bellacerka, raised there, and still live there. The Serb positions are still there, they're still open, they have not been covered. And until I leave, I will not allow anyone to cover them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, from Bela Crkva to Celine, how many roads are there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One and a half kilometre --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's only one road from Bellacerka, but the road here is -- turns like this. But from Bellacerka, it is a straight road. At the exit of Bellacerka, you can actually see Celine; it's in a straight line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ackerman, on this map it looks as though there are two roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I think this map was put together by UNMIK or KFOR or somebody like that, probably properly done. I don't know. I think the Prosecution has represented it to us as accurate. I suspect it probably is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Aren't there two roads going from Bela Crkva to Celina, sir?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is one road that goes to Celine from Bellacerka. And from Rahovec, there is another road that goes to the place where the tanks were positioned; a road that goes from Rahovec to Celine. And from Bellacerka, there is only one road that goes to Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is there any way you can mark on this map where the tanks were positioned after they left your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tanks were positioned above Naim Fetoshi's house. I really don't understand this map, because this road to Brestovc, it's not close to Bellacerka. Bernjaqa is only 500 metres away from Bellacerka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want a shot taken of this map --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bernjaqa is adjacent to Bellacerka, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before we do this, Mr. Popaj, you'll see on the map a railway line. You see the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- see the railway line. And you can see the -- and you can see --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you can see the Belaje stream which flows under the railway line. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I can see it very well, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just above that you can see that there's sort of a yellow -- yellow-orange coloured line that joins Bela Crkva to Celina, which looks like a road, it's meant to be a road. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this road from Bellacerka does not take you to Celine, and the railway track are the same distance -- are further from Bellacerka --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- than Celine. Bernjaqa is 500 metres far from the house in Bellacerka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, above that line there is another one with a sort of bend on it which also goes on the map from Bela Crkva to Celine, which looks like another road. Now, is that what you would say was the road to Celine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This road does not take you to Celine. This road does not exist at all. The road from the village of Bellacerka takes you straight to Celine. This road to Rahovec and to Bernjaqa, above here were the positions, 150 metres far from the positions, while this road here from Bellacerka to Celine is not correct. It should be a straight line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ackerman, are there no photographs that you could, perhaps, use that might assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, Your Honour. That one photograph doesn't show all of the area that's necessary to make this clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You have made, Mr. Witness, some red dots. I don't know. It looks like you made at least three red dots up along that main road. Is that where the Serb positions were, by your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be the road that goes to Rahovec. Here is Naim Fetoshi's house, and above his house were the positions. It should be somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Draw a circle around that area that you have designated as where the positions were.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, on this hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. You made a small circle just north of the road, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Now let's do a screen shot of this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Above the main road that goes to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Screen shot, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC99, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just in order to maybe assist with the confusion about the roads. We just checked the legend in the Kosovo atlas, and the fine red line is said to be a seasonal road/track, so that may explain some of the confusion, maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I doubt if it does because it's clear that the witness envisages that there is a road from Bela Crkva to Celine, and what it can be other than one of these seasonal tracks is difficult to see here. But you'll have a chance to deal with that in re-examination, if you wish. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, the last question I want to ask you about this map, while it's still on the screen, you told us in your statement that from these bunkers there was automatic fire directed across the top of your village. They were shooting over the tops of the houses as a warning, you believed, that you should leave your houses. Now, from where they were shooting over the top of your village, what is there over there on the other side of your village in the direction they were shooting? What's located over there? Just fields and that stream and things?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the bunkers were, it's only field there. There's no stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you didn't see any KLA soldiers leaving your village and heading out that direction, the direction in which those shots were being fired? You didn't see that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no way I could go there, because this was five or six days before the 25th. There was no way that I could go and check. From the moment the NATO bombing started on the night of the 24th, the bursts of fire did not stop. And, as I said, this map does not represent the real positions of the villages. The road that goes to Celine is a road through fields, not used by animals.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, over the next several days, after the 25th of March --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you do, Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Popaj, you say that the road to Celine goes through fields. Now, when you say in your statement, "the tanks moved off," they were not on that road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is a road that goes to Rahovec, that connects to the road to Rahovec and takes you to the hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm now further confused, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me ask you again. I know you think this map is totally inaccurate. Is there any way you can give us just a -- an approximation of where the tanks parked, after they went through your village? Can you find a place on that map that's anywhere representative of where you saw those tanks parked on a hill?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that not what the red circle is supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. The red circle are the holes that were dug by the Serb forces. The tanks went to Celina, he said, parked themselves on a hill over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, parked on a hill overlooking Celina. That's what you have to interrupt, and I thought that was the witness's interpretation but I may be wrong. You should clarify what the red circle is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, the red circle is where the bunkers were dug, isn't it. And from where the firing was coming?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The trenches were above Bellacerka, while the tanks that went in the direction of Celine. If you have a photograph, you can see a cow-shed there where they positioned themselves. It's above Celine and Bellacerka. Here is Bellacerka; here is Celine. They were on a hill between Bellacerka and Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Halfway between or what?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this hill, you can see Bellacerka and Celine on this side, and you can see Nagavc on the other side. The positions are still there, can be seen there. The stable or the cow-shed where they were positioned can still be seen; it's still there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And to get to that position when they left the village, did they go initially in the direction of Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They did not go on a main road to Rahovec, but on the one that took you to the vineyards above Rahovec. It's a small road that takes you to the vineyards. And that road takes a turn and goes to the cow-shed where they took position. It's a bit of a hill with oak trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can't figure out a way to clarify this any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. It's just possible that the description we've been given is the upper-most of these two farm roads. But it's far from clear, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to go to another subject now. After the 25th of March, you talk about in your statement - and I don't want to go into any detail at all; this should be a fairly statement for you to answer - you talk about finding and burying a number of bodies at very locations. My only question about that is: Were you able to make a determination when you observed these bodies whether they were killed by fire-arms or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them were shot by fire-arms. The casings of the automatic rifles were there, and I showed them to the investigators when we got the bodies out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to know. After you'd given your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, do you remember giving a statement to an investigating judge in Prizren in a case against a gentleman by the name of Andjelko Kolasinac from Orahovac? Do you remember doing that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: According to a document that the OTP provided to us, what you said in that interrogation, in that statement, to this investigating judge with regard to the matters we've just been discussing was this: "On the morning of 25 March 1999, around 3.00, I heard and saw Serbian police and military troops entering the village of Bellacerke. They arrived up to the village mosque and then moved in a direction of the hill above the village. I woke up earlier and asked my family members to prepare leave the village." Now, nowhere that I was able to find in that statement that you gave to this investigating judge did you say anything at all about tanks coming to your village, did you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They never asked. I didn't give this statement. It was my wife. My wife was ill on the day, so I went in her stead. She was about to give birth, and so it was me who went to give that statement. Fidaije Popaj, that's the name on the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, the statement I have says the statement was given by Sabri Popaj. Did you take a statement she'd written and just read it to them; is that what you did?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife had to go to trial in Prizren because they'd taken the son out of our hands, and we didn't have a doctor with us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. This is a question I ask just out of curiosity. I think you told us there were 2.800 people that lived in your village. On page 6685 of the transcript of your testimony in Milosevic, the transcript says there were 5.000 cattle in your village. Is that really true? Were there really 5.000 cattle in a village of 2.800 people?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. It was true because I had over 40. I've got 32 to this day and I had 180 sheep. I haven't mentioned that in my statement, but even today you've got there over 1.500 sheep.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Who is Muharrem Popaj from Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muharrem Popaj used to be my uncle; he's no longer alive, my father's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And his father's name was Hidajet Popaj?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hidajet Popaj. The son was Najit Popaj, not Muharrem Popaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I have information that there was a --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Najit Popaj is my aunt's son. My mother and his mother are sisters. We live in adjacent houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me tell you some information I have. I have information that Hidaj Popaj, H-i-d-a-j, Popaj, was arrested by the KLA and that his son, Muharrem Popaj, was making efforts in various places to try to get him released. Do you know anything about this Popaj person being arrested by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this yesterday. He wasn't arrested by the KLA. He went to see his mother in Pristina, and he was kidnapped by Serbian police and disappeared. We found him last year. His remains were brought to me and then he was buried. And that came from the mortuary at Rahovec. I took his remains and buried it. It's about a year since then. We buried him last December.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had asked yesterday for a check on page 84, line 16, of the transcript, as to whether the translation was accurate or not. It appears in the transcript and I was hoping I'd have that this morning. Apparently it's not been finished yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it should be. I was assured it would be. Just give us a second to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's apparently not complete, so you can have a chance later. Hopefully it will be completed before the cross-examination in total is finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. I think what I'll do is defer a series of questions that I have then on that issue until that's available, if that's okay with Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Popaj. My name is Branko Lukic. I have quite a few questions for you. Could you please focus and give me as brief answers as possible, whenever you can. Let me ask you this first: Do you distinguish colours?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the registrar to show us P93, page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, yesterday, when you spoke about this photograph, on page 38, line 17, the Prosecutor asks you: [In English] "And the camouflage uniform, which colour camouflage was it?" [Interpretation] In lines 18 to 19, you answer: [In English] "It was the colour you see in the photograph but it was lighter than this." [Interpretation] Could you see that colour on police uniforms, and is it the same colour you can see on the drapes behind the Judges?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A bit lighter and camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it is the same colour as the colour of the drapes behind the Judges.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same colour, but the clothes themselves, the uniform, was camouflage. It was not uniform like that. Show them to me on the screen here. I can't describe them just like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. On page 45, you spoke of killings near the bridge and say that people were forced to take their jackets off, that the jackets were searched. How long did this search and robbing, thieving, from the jackets last?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there myself; I was hidden. I dared not get up, so I stayed there, near the hole that was filled with water. I don't know how long it lasted. I never checked my watch. And I still -- I still have the jacket of my son which he left there on that bank; I still have it at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you looking in that direction?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was looking in that direction, but I haven't -- I was not able to see them when they put them in the direction of the stream; I saw them on the banks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly, since you were looking in that direction, how long the searching of those people lasted.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I didn't check my watch. I saw them when they put them above the railway tracks, put in a line and made to take off their clothes. Some of the clothes were left behind; some were put on. And I still have the clothes of the people who were killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, when I ask you how long something lasted, could you just answer me how long it took rather than describe the whole event, because you have already done that in your statement. You said that you were even looking through binoculars. How many people did you see on the bridge and near the bridge at that moment?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to count them. About half the village was there. They separated the women from the others, and some were left in the last group and taken to the direction of Xerxe. Only the young children were left near Belaje, and the young children and the women were sent in the direction of the tracks. And people were able to tell who they were. Some are still alive, some elderly people still. My mother, my wife, my father, they were all separated. I have no idea how long it took. I know when we were executed because I could hear the volleys of all the bursts of gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that moment were you able to see that large group of people at the moment when the people were searched, when their jackets were taken off? Were civilians present there at the same time?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilians who were separated, yes, they were. But they were unable to see them take their clothes off. It was only the mother, the wife, and my father who saw them when they were executed. And I have pointed the sign where they were. There's a sign there, there's a permanent sign. Sometimes they take it off, but I go there and re-insert it, put it back there. It's near the railway track.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'll ask you something regarding page 60 of your statement. It concerns the moment when, as you say, all the three mosques were blown up, something that you saw. On page 60, line 19, you say: [In English] "In the field between Celine and Bellacerka." [Interpretation] The next page, 61, line 5, you say: [In English] "We were there at the side of the mountain. That's what we call it." [Interpretation] So my question is: Were you in the field or were you on top of a hill when you were observing this? Which of these is true?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at Breg; it was near. That is my field. That's the field, three and a half hectares; two are on the hilly bit, and the rest of it is further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So is it a hill or a field?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Half of it is a plain field and the rest of it is hilly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Listen to the answer, Mr. Lukic. It's a field, part of which is on a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was trying to get from him whether he was in the field or on the hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question is: Was it a hill or a field? That may a mistranslation, but it's what came through to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try again, Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popaj, at that moment were you on a hill or in a field?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my field. It begins on -- and is a plain field, and then the hill begins. And I wasn't up or down; I was at the foot. That's where I was and that's where I could observe from. There were those, me and the others, who did the exhumation in that particular spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that moment, is that what you're trying to say, at the moment when these mosques were blown up, you were not alone; there was somebody else there with you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 79, you speak of those three members of the KLA from your village who existed, as you were told, but you never learned their names. Because, as you say, you were in the mountains with cattle until 1998. When did you climb down from the mountains together with your cattle?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that every year I go up to the Bjeshket e Jasharit up on the top of the mountain. I've done that since 1973. I did it this year. I stayed there for about two years. I go there every year on the 21st of May and I return on the 20th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said you climbed down from the mountains in 1998. When I'm interested in something that you did in earlier years, I will ask you that. In 1998, when did you come back from the mountain?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that every year we descend there from the 20th of September to the 20th of October. This year, for instance, we did it on the 20th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the 20th of October until the 24th of March when, let's say, the NATO bombing began and the 25th, when this happened in your village, in those six months you did not find out the names of those three men. Is that your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't interested. In the very morning I take the animals out. I did have sheep then; I don't have them anymore. We were too scared to go to the hills over there, but we went in the direction of Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We'll come back to this. You know that there was a book published in Kosovo titled, "Fenikset e Lirise." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't read; I'm not a politician. I don't read books.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You followed the trial of now late Slobodan Milosevic, and you listened to the testimony of Bozidar Delic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. When I came here to testify in the Milosevic trial, I came straight from the top of the mountain. I left the animals there and came here to testify on the 28th of May, 2002, and returned on the 14th of June, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that with the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 29th of June, 2005, you discussed the testimony of Bozidar Delic, including the book titled, "Phoenixes of Freedom," "Fenikset e Lirise," in Albanian. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen that book.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Is then your evidence today that you did not speak to investigators of the OTP on the 29th of June, 2005?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember speaking to them in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. An investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor, Ljubomir Jozefciak - at least according to the documents we received from the Prosecution and which is entered in the system under 6D105 - it is said that in this report we received from the Prosecution, we have comments made by Mr. Sabri Popaj that he made after being shown the publication "Fenikset e Lirise," published in Pristina in 2002. In this statement, it is said that you discussed the book and the affiliation of certain members of your family to the KLA, as stated in the said book. Do you now remember this conversation with the investigators of the Prosecution, Mr. Popaj?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember seeing someone, but I didn't ask whether he was an investigator. I do remember now. I don't know his name. I don't know who it was, and he asked, "Why have we written somewhere at the graveyards that someone was a Martyr," and in fact they weren't. And that has been taken off the tombstones, and I know what you're referring to. Yes, that one came to see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you, not at all what I mean. I'm just asking you if you remember the conversation.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand it now. I do remember it now. I don't know the of that person --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back to that later. I'll ask you something different now. In your statement of the 12th June 1999, you say that you gave food and money to the KLA. Did anybody force you to do that, or did you do that of your own will?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of our own free will; the whole of the village did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the villagers from your village help the KLA in the same way?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who had something to give; those who didn't, didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now have to ask a couple of questions that our Chamber designates as the Milosevic-style question, but that will take only a few minutes. Do you know that the attacks against the police in your village started already on the 18th of March, 1998, when a patrol of the traffic police was attacked?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you claim that on the 18th of March, 1998, there was no such attack in your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. And do you know that on the night of the 18th of July, 1998, in the village of Bela Crkva, there was several terrorist attacks against the police, using automatic weapons, rocket-launchers, mortars, light machine-guns, and snipers, on which occasion the KLA blocked the road from Zerze to Orahovac. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that particular time I was up in the mountains, and I know that the road to Rahovec had been sealed off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who sealed off that road?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there; I said that. But I know on that particular day the whole of the village had left. And on that particular day they killed my wife's uncle, Ibrahim Popaj, born in 1916, Hajzizi Popaj, Hamita Popaj, and Ravia Popaj. I was up in the mountains. I say that, and I returned after, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We see that you say that the population of the village moved that day. Also in the Milosevic trial, on page 6683, line 2, you say: [In English] "Has positions on the 22nd of March and 80 per cent of the people had already left."

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left on March the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't yet asked you anything. In which part of the village were the remaining 20 per cent of the inhabitants of your village who, as you say, remained after the 24th of March, 1999, or the 20 per cent remaining were scattered all over the village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were on the lower part of the village, not on the side where the bunkers and positions were. It's towards my house where -- as the photograph shows, they were all there, whilst the upper part of the village had all left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say there was no KLA in the village. You also say on page English version 3, paragraph 2; Albanian version page 3, paragraph 4, you say that the policemen and soldiers fired above roof-tops, and you understood that as a warning that you should leave the village. Is it the case that in the forests overlooking the village there were members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no members of the KLA. It could be seen when the volleys of gun-fire were fired from there, and you could see from the village of Bellacerka where the first houses started burning. And this was the house of Xhem Gashi and Ymer Gashi. These were the first houses to be burned on that particular morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It suffices to say you assert that there was no KLA in the forest overlooking your village.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not in the village. There was KLA but not in the village of KLA. They were where the positions were, and they had units in Drenovc and Reti. Drenovc is 14 kilometres, while Reti, 16 kilometres, far from my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. In your statement you also say that you were helping the Zhuniqi family as well as the Spahiu family to cross the river -- to cross the river Belaje. Did you do this regularly? Were you tasked with helping people cross the stream?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not my task. But as I was there, I heard the cry of this child and went in that direction to see who was there. So I saw the Zhuniqi and Spahiu family there, and I helped them cross. And Xhemail Spahiu did not cross but he remained on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether you were tasked with that; you said no, and that is the answer to my question. Thank you. How come you were not with your family on that day?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't want to go. I wanted to stay there because my cattle was at home. When I went to help the Spahiu family, after that I returned again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you say that after that you were in the field, close to an electricity pole.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you allow for the possibility that the electricity pole is much closer to the river than you have marked it on the map. Electricity poles are basically by the river itself.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The electricity pylon is still there, where I was hiding. We did not remove it. It's on the field, on my field. And the hole from where we water the field is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is precisely what I wanted to ask you. In the field there are some holes, dug-outs. Is that what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an irrigation canal. The pylon has been cut, but it's about 1 metre tall. I did not remove it. It's on my field, and I go to work on that field every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you again: Are there any holes in the field, and did you use them to hide there? Or were you standing out in the open?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can find holes at every 50 metres, where the outlets to start the water are. They're about 1 metre or 1 metre and 20 centimetres deep, and we go down there to turn on the outlets for the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, in your view, these are not shelters which had been dug to be used by the members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not dug by the KLA. They were dug by the people who built the Radonjic system, the irrigation system. Every field has these holes, the entire plain, up to Vandoviqe [phoen]. I can even tell you, if necessary, who built that system.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. I envisaged, Mr. Lukic, that we would go on until ten to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's perfectly fine with me. I just wanted to check. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll do an hour and a half before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At page 3 in the English, paragraph 6 - and in the Albanian, this is paragraph 3, page 4, as well as page 3, paragraph 4 of the B/C/S - you talk about the approach of some armed Serbs. This was a group of 14 people. These policemen, did they follow the people from the same direction or did they come from another direction?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can show you on the map from which direction they came. I can mark it with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can tell us whether they came from the direction of Bela Crkva or from some other direction?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction of Bellacerka, and they followed the line of the Belaje stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, they did not come from the direction of Rogovo.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They came from Bellacerka village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, if someone were to say that they came from the direction of Rogovo, they would not be telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody came from Rugova. On the main road Prizren-Gjakova, they were there, the police and army, the Serbian police and army, and they were firing from there. But they did not go to the scene, to the spot itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm trying to compare your statement to that of Isuf Zhuniqi. Thank you. Next, you describe a group of people by the railway bridge. I'm interested in the following: What was the position of your son Shendet, when he was shot, since you say you saw that moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not see them shoot at him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm actually objecting to that. I think the witness did say explicitly in his testimony that he did not see the moment when the men were shot; he just saw his son when they were searched.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I, if you look at the second-last paragraph on page 4, which was changed, I understand that he saw his brother being executed and the position of his son was unclear after that change was made. So is there a reason why he can't explore that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No, I think there is no reason why it can't be explored, but I think it's not correct to put to the witness that he said that he saw his son being shot, because he didn't say that yesterday, to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, could you clarify that, please, with the witness, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popaj, did you see your son being fired at?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not when they fired at him. But when they took the group of people to the position where they executed, that's when I could see them. But when they took them down to the stream itself, I could no longer see that because the bank was steep.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw your brother being shot at; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They executed all of them at the same time. When I went close to that area, I found my son killed near my brother Nesim, while Agon --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the last name of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, you didn't see your brother being shot either?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any of them when they were shot at, but I could hear the gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You saw policemen with bands around their heads, on their foreheads. Did you used to see any other policemen with the sweat-bands before?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not with scarves. I saw them with scarves on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I could not see them. And when they executed Fetoshi, they were with their faces turned towards Fetoshi. I could only see their backs. There's no way I could recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw their backs. Did you see any insignia on their uniforms, before or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see their insignia. I could see them talk on the radios because they had radios.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also state that you saw policemen wearing white surgical gloves. Did you indeed see policemen wearing white surgical gloves?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found the gloves there when we exhumed the bodies, and we found syringes there. These gloves were collected by the investigators who were present when the exhumation took place. You can ask them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not an answer to the question, Mr. Popaj. The question was: Did you actually see policemen wearing white surgical gloves, which is what your statement says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found them near the bodies, because as they were leaving, after having executed the group, they threw the gloves. And we also found syringes there and injections, and we gave everything to the investigators involved in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you actually see them throwing the gloves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said in my statement that I was told by Sari Zhuniqi, who was hiding a little bit further up. I saw these gloves when the bodies were exhumed, together with the cartridge cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, which paragraph is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's paragraph in English version, Your Honour, page 3, paragraph 6; in Albanian version, page 4, paragraph 3. It's the last sentence of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the answer now is that he did not see this, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- this is what he has subsequently concluded from what was subsequently found.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statement you say that the shooting in village lasted not only all day, all that day, but for an entire month. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, until the 4th of May, when they burned the last houses belonging to Muharrem Zhuniqi. And on that day, they forced the people of Xerxe out of their houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did the shooting last all day long, since there were no civilians in the village, there was no KLA presence in the village, in your words? Were Serbs shooting at each other?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were shooting in case there was someone there. They would come in in a truck who belonged to a Gashi, and they could load that truck with things that they plundered. They took the truck and never returned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it your transcript today that the Serbs who were there opened fire on empty Albanian houses or directed their fire against the nearby forest or at the burned-down houses? What was they shooting at?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went back to my burned house on many occasions, and I could recognise Serbs from Rahovec. I have not mentioned their names, but they entered the house and they plundered. And I know exactly by name who stole my truck. And he called me last year and told me that I could go and get my truck in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation] --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, for a period of a month until the 4th of May, what were they shooting at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were not shooting at anyone. They were shooting in the air; the thought that there might be someone in the village. They would go inside houses and loot them. I could see them looting the house of Muharrem Zhuniqi. They would load the truck with the things they have looted, and they would drive off. And on the last day they also carried the things that they had looted in my vehicle. They stole three vehicles; my truck, Muharrem Gashi's truck, and another person's truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't ask you about the presence of the KLA, since you said that you were in the mountains after March. I think we spoke about the 18th of June, 1998. In this case we intend to show - and this is our Defence's position which I'm putting to you now - that your village and its surrounding area was a stronghold of the KLA. This can be deducted from the Albanian documents that we possess. One of the documents confirming that is the very book we began discussing, the name of which is "Fenikset e Lirise." In that book, among other members of the KLA who were killed, there are also the names of some of your family members. You mentioned that in the statement we received from the OTP, when you spoke to their investigator on the 29th of October, 2006 -- no, I apologise. It was in June 2002. At page 23 of the book - and it bears the ERN number 00088083 - there is a person by the name of Alban R. Popaj mentioned there. In the statement concerning your interview with an OTP investigator dated the 29th of June, 2005, you mentioned this person, and you said he was your brother's son; your brother's name was Remzi. Is that correct? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He asked me that they appeared in the book as KLA members, and I told him they were not. And I also told him I didn't know who wrote that book.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This exhibit is number D105. If you wish to see it, I can show you some of the pages of the document, although I don't believe there is any need for it for the time being. For the transcript, the exhibit number is 6D104. Thank you. On the same list in the same book there is a name of Nesim S. Popaj at page 75 of the book. He was from Bela Crkva. You identified him as your brother when you spoke to the OTP investigators. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told him that he was my brother, but they were not KLA soldiers. And this is what I told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the same list at page 94, there is a Shendet S. Popaj, and this was your son. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among the KLA members from your village, at least according to the book, bearing the last name of Popaj, we also have the following persons: At page 67, Mehmet I. Popaj, you identified him as your neighbour; at page 86, Sahit V. Popaj, another neighbour of yours; at page 98, Xhavit S. Popaj, born 1969; and at page 111, Kreshnik Popaj. You know all of these people, and they were all your relatives and neighbours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are my relatives and neighbours, my first cousins and so on. But this has wrote -- someone has wrote this book and made them look as if they were KLA soldiers, but they were not. How can my son be a member of the KLA when he was only 17? The same can be said for Kreshnik. Even my youngest son was listed in the book. How could he have been a KLA member when he was only 14?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, we will take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You should bear in mind what we've said earlier about the extent to which, in cross-examination, when time is limited, some issues should be explored. I acknowledge, though, that obtaining confirmation of the identity of certain people as related to the witness is important so that they can be tied to the schedule. But on the general proposition about the presence of the KLA in the village, the witness's position is clear; whether it's true is another matter, but it's clear. So we'll resume at 11.15. Mr. Popaj, the usher will show you where to wait while we have our break; it will be a break of about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness comes in, if I may. Why I'm exploring all these names, among other things, is that you ordered the Prosecution to revise the list and to see whether to leave the list as it is or not or change -- or to change it. So I think that's our last chance, actually, to check with this witness if he knows the identity of some inhabitants of his village enumerated as the KLA fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I acknowledged that when I spoke at the end of the last session. But it's quite a different thing to invite the Prosecution to amend the list to reflect all who were killed or delete any who were not killed from suggesting amendment because a person killed may have had a particular status or have been doing a certain thing. That will be a matter for us to judge. The schedule is simply a reflection of the people killed, and you're not, I think, disputing that these people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All I'm suggesting is that sort of detail I understand you pursuing, but the generality is of doubtful value, bearing in mind how often the witness has made his position on that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will try now, Mr. Popaj, to speed things up, and I will only ask you whether the following people are familiar to you, who are also designated in the same book as members of the KLA, and it is stated that they were born and died in Bela Crkva: Agim E. Kelmendi; Fatos Zhuniqi; Kasim S. Zhuniqi; Eshref Zhuniqi; and Ramiz Krasniqi. Do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know Ramiz Krasniqi. There is no Krasniqi in Bellacerka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Could I ask for a clarification, please. Is the witness saying that he knows the Zhuniqis?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should I ask the witness or are you asking him, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: You can go ahead and ask. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are the other persons whose names I read out to you familiar to you as residents of your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know them. Fatos Zhuniqi was a professor of the English language and he continued teaching until the 24th. He was not a member of the KLA. Eshref Zhuniqi was an elderly man. Kasim Zhuniqi or Kelmendi was not even in the village; he wasn't killed in the village either, Agim Kelmendi. I have no idea where he was killed. And the rest of them, no, they were not members of the KLA. Fatos Zhuniqi was executed alongside his own son, 14 years of age, Labinoti.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. In the third category of KLA fighters who have fallen, according to this book, we find names of people who are not from Bela Crkva, but it is stated next to their names that they died in the fighting in Bela Crkva, that they got killed in the fighting. So I'm asking you: Did you have occasion to meet any one of them? Mrs. Afridita S. Bokshin, did you know her?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Saim a-Gashi from Drenovaca?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hadija M. Spahiu from Rahovec?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found Hadija Spahiu at the house of Nurije Kelmendi. She was killed there and I buried her. I did not recognise who she was. I found her. She'd been raped and massacred. And only after the exhumation it was possible to identify her as Hadija Spahiu, from Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Eparem A. Thaqi?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He doesn't come from my village. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He is from Landovica, but he got killed in your village.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Perparem A. Thaqi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sakip X. Bellaqa from Patacani.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no family with the surname of Bellaqa there. We don't have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. That's a man from Pataqane, but according to this book, he got killed in the fighting in your village; that's why I am asking if you had ever met him.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never knew him. There are some Bellaqas in the upper Pataqane. There are two Pataqanes. And I did not know this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. There are several more names but I am not going through them with you. In your statement given to an investigator of the Tribunal on the 29th of June, 2005, you state that it is impossible for your son Agon Popaj to be named in that book because he had never been a member of the KLA. He wasn't even 14 at the time. I did not find the name of your son Agon Popaj in this book. I don't know if you did and why you mentioned him, too, when you discussed this book.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator told me that in that book there are all kinds of names, including your small -- your little child, your little son. And I told him that it wasn't possible for Skender or Agon to be there. And I asked him who had written about it but he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that he put himself on the KLA list as a volunteer, although he wasn't even 14. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. He was at school, and his teacher of English was Fatos Zhuniqi. He taught him in year 7 of the primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. When you were burying those people, why did you decide to bury them in a mass grave? Why didn't you bury them in individual graves?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was impossible for us to take them to the graveyard because of the police, so we had to bury them in the night, on the night of the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That night, when you were burying those people, were there any members of the Serb forces in your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the middle of the village and up in the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You marked some bodies by placing their names in little bottles; however, you marked only 17 bodies in this way. Why not all?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't enough bottles going around, and that is why we put pieces of paper with their names. Every one of them had a piece of paper. There were only 17 bottles and we used them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page, English version, 7, paragraph 3; in Albanian, page 9, paragraph, you say the following: "Feim Popaj, the son of my uncle, one of the survivors from the massacre at the stream, told me that he recognised two of the policemen who did the shooting and killing. Those were Zlatko Bozanic and another one who's first name is Dejan." You say, "I know these two policemen or I recognised these two policemen," but then you go on to say, "I didn't recognise them at the time because I was too far away." Did you see those men at that moment or heard from someone else that they were there?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement says that the news came from my uncle's son, Feimi, who was able to recognise them and people were lined up to the to the executed. Zlatko Bozanic was the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is Zlatko Bozanic from Opterusa?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know that Serbs from Opterusa were expelled back in 1998?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Serbs from Opterusa were kidnapped and killed in 1998, and the assaults were led by KLA commander Haxhi Mazreku, who was, by the way, a member of the military police of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't know who Haxhi Mazreku was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1998 Serbs were kidnapped and killed from Opterusa, a place where this Bosko Bozanic comes from?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can ask Muzreku to come here and explain about it. I told you that during 1998 I was not there, up until October.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. So after October you did not hear of anything like that happening, or maybe you know that something happened before October?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about; it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. I'll abandon this area. We'll move on to something different. In your statement on page 7 of the English version, paragraph 7; and page 10, paragraph 1 of the Albanian version you say: "Hysni Zhuniqi and his nephews, Mehdi Zhuniqi and Akim Zhuniqi" - and there's one unintelligible part of the translation - "I suppose and believe that those people were killed at the time that I heard that shooting five minutes after the first execution that I'd seen. I left those bodies where they were and went back to Xerxe." Among those names you include Hysni Zhuniqi from Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was six people all in all. Yufan Popaj and Sadet Popaj, first cousins; Hysni Zhuniqi, Delvish; Hajram Labega; Memohmdi Zhuniqi; Negev Zhuniqi. Six people in all. This was on a different day, Muharrem Zhuniqi told me: "I heard the volleys of gun-fire, but I couldn't see them being killed. After the burial, the people killed in the big massacre I returned and saw the bodies of these people. It is not on the same day. I did hear the volleys of gun-fire, but I wasn't aware that they'd been killed. I found them on the day that I buried them, that is on the 27th of March."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you then. Among those people, according to you, there was Hysni Zhuniqi?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Hysni Zhuniqi born in 1937 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's twice, Mr. Lukic, you've made that point, and it's a quite unnecessary proposition to put. And it leads to the witness going on at length explaining yet again what is obvious to us all or adding a little bit more. It's better if you put a question, rather than a proposition prior to the question, and incorporate the proposition into your question; then we won't have this time being consumed by unnecessary repetition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know that Hysni Zhuniqi from Bela Crkva succumbed to his injuries in the health care centre in Prizren. And he was killed by NATO bombs on the 2nd of April, 1999, together with ten persons, out of whom these were identified: Qazim Krasniqi, his father's name Isa, from Mala Hoca; Makmuud Krasniqi from Mala Hoca; and Elshan Hysni from Nagales village.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hysni Juniqi, born in 1971, he was the one who was killed, while Hysni Sulejman Zhuniqi is a different person and he was born in 1937. He was buried in Prizren, but I exhumed the body in Prizren. And I buried him on July the 5th, alongside the group that was exhumed in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was guided by your observation that there were no two persons with the same name in your village, and I supposed --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first name is not the same, though. The first one was called Husen not Hysni. Husen and Hysni are quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have the same spelling of the name for both of them, but never mind. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have got it here in these papers, on the original, and I've got every detail recorded of the burial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, which one is Husen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Husen was killed in Nagavc. Hysni died in the canal alongside six other people. And the name is Husen Ahmet Zhuniqi; Ahmet being his father's name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The name I have for Nagavc is Hysni, but we can clarify it hopefully in some other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time you were moving towards Celina, towards Zerze. Is it your testimony today that on the 25th, the 26th, the 27th, the 28th, the 29th, and all the way up to the 2nd of April there was no fighting in the area of your village and those other villages between Serb forces and the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't. There were no people either in the village, with the exception of the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'll just ask you one more thing. In the Milosevic trial, when you spoke about the moment when you saw 12 policemen, you say that on the other side of the river you did not see how many policemen there were; however, the fact is they were paramilitaries from Serbia. Did you see paramilitaries, in fact, there?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir. It was the paramilitaries who did the execution of the 74 people from the village; it wasn't me who did the execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just come back to the moment when you were going through the border-crossing. Five of you handed in your documents. Other members of your group did not produce documents. May we conclude that at that moment neither you, nor anyone else in your group were searched for documents. The only documents taken from you were those you handed in yourselves.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked us to surrender our IDs. I didn't have them. There were some five people; most of them are women and children. And there's only five of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you were not searched; that's only -- that's the only thing I want to know.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They just chucked them away and burned those five IDs that they took from people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac -- Mr. Cepic, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think I will take this witness, but I believe Mr. Ackerman wants to finish his examination before me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, I have just very little more to ask you about, and before I ask you another question, I have to give you information. The way the system works here is there is an audio-recording, or video- and audio-recording, made of your testimony at the time you give it, so we have an audio record of what you said in answer to questions. You might recall yesterday that I asked the Judge to have that audio record checked with regard to what you said about the shell fragments or bomb fragments from Nagavc. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And so that was done, and what we're told by the translators today is what you said was this: "It is a clear proof that the fragments of the bomb exist, are there. We have them. They were in Nagavc village, where the bombing occurred. We have them, the fragments of the shell. I have them at home." And then you talk about when the bombing happened and you say: "We have the shells there. The investigators themselves have seen them." Later, in your testimony yesterday, you said, no, you didn't have those fragments at your home, that they were in the home, in Nagavc, of a gentleman named Feim Elshani. My question is: Why did you tell us you had them at your home if you didn't have them there? What was your purpose in telling that untruth?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said -- I did not mean me, in person. I said, "We do have them," and "we" means many more people, which means in our houses. But they are being stored at Feim Elshani's house. He's the one who came to testify on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mean me, in person; I meant we, in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you know, the thing you can't do is challenge your own words that we have recorded here in this courtroom, and your own words were, "I have them at home," and then you told us that the investigators had seen them, presumably at your home. That's all not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ [Resumed]
