In your statement - this is page 4 of the English statement, the second paragraph from the bottom; also page 4 of the Serb version of the statement; and it's the sixth paragraph - you say that on the 27th of March, 1999, at around 8.30 p.m., "I went out and saw villagers who were gathered in a centre of it." Was it in the evening or in the morning that you went out and saw these villagers gathered there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: It was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, these were the villagers of Drenoc and you said there were four other -- there were four families from the village of Sllup. Do you know why these villagers gathered there that morning? Did they tell you why they were there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: It is true that there were four families from the village of Sllup as well, and they gathered there because they told us that was police who came from the village and told them to leave the village automatically, all at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. And the villagers from your own village, Drenoc, were gathered there. Did they say why they were gathered there, in the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: They converged in the centre because police had forced them to evacuate on account or the pretext that they had to, because NATO was about to bomb them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how many villagers were gathered there that morning, when you went outside there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: At this stage there were 520 villagers from my village and 37 that came from the village of Sllup.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you speak, as a village supervisor, with any of the policemen who were telling people to leave their homes or who were forcing people from their homes, or did any of them speak to you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did speak to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: "Mr. Teacher," they said, "you should leave the village and go beyond the asphalted road and make your way towards the other villages."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What did you understand them to mean when they said "beyond the asphalted road"?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: What they meant was for us to evacuate the village, and I cannot say here what their ultimate intention might have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did you know these policemen before? Could you say where these policemen were from?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. One came from Peje. I don't know his name. The other -- of the other two, one was called Ahmet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And where were they from, the other two?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: One of the other two came from Decan, from the police station at Decan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask for clarification of one thing. On page 4, that very first paragraph dealing with the 27th of March, Mr. Stamp, there's a sentence at the end, "Local Albanian policemen told us not to leave the village because nothing would happen to us."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's still part of the evidence, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You what?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I intend to get to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you say the people gathered because they had been instructed to leave by police officers from Pec and Decan, and you said in your statement, as just indicated by His Honour, that "local ... policemen told us not to leave the village because nothing would happen to us." Can you explain this, please.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. The police who came from that neighbourhood had been chosen by the Decan police; the other two were local policemen, both of them Albanians. And they asked us not to leave the village; however, we disobeyed their advice and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So I take it from your answer that the police who came from Decani told the villagers to leave, but the local Albanian police in the area asked you not to leave.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, because they thought they held -- they held a higher position. In fact, what they were was simply my co-villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said in your statement - and I'm looking at the English version, at the bottom of page 4, going on to page 5 - that you set out to Carrabreg in order to ask the police at the check-point at Carrabreg if the villagers could pass through that check-point. I take it from that that you and the villagers had decided to leave the village. Why did you decide to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: We decided to leave the village because they forced us to. At that point I went to Carrabreg, where Serbian police had a check-point at the crossroads at Carrabreg. And, on behalf of the village, I went there to request that we be left to move beyond the check-point towards the village of Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stamp, we will have to interrupt there, I'm afraid. It's unfortunate, but there are technical reasons why we can't continue this afternoon, albeit the court's available. Well, Mr. Mazrekaj, I'm afraid we have to finish there for the day because we don't have the facility to carry on in this courtroom today. We will have to resume your evidence tomorrow. For that purpose, you will have to be back here at 9.00 to re-commence giving evidence. Overnight, please do not speak to anyone, anyone at all, about anything to do with your evidence, either the evidence you've given or the evidence you will give. You can talk about anything else, but the evidence is absolutely off limits to your discussions.. So could you please leave the courtroom now with the usher and we'll see you back here tomorrow again at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
